newsitem.title: USA: U.S. homes not tuned in to Internet TV, survey says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. homes not tuned in to Internet TV, survey says.

text.p: Despite the hoopla over the launch of WebTV and other products providing simpler and cheaper access to the Internet by television, a survey published Monday found most U.S. households did not intend to tune in.

Only 4 percent of America's 98 million households currently plan to purchase a TV Internet device, according to a telephone survey of nearly 7,000 home consumers conducted by the San Jose-based market research firm Dataquest.
Some 3 percent were undecided and 93 percent had no intention of purchasing such devices, which are being marketed as a cheaper alternative to computers costing $1,000 or more.

"As it stands right now, with the products that are currently being offered in the market, we think the potential for it is relatively small," said Van Baker, director and principal analyst of Dataquest's digital consumer program.

The Dataquest survey comes just weeks after the launch of WebTV, a set-top box which enables consumers to access the Internet through WebTV Networks Inc.'s service, and at the height of the pre-Christmas shopping season.
The report contrasted with a Yankelovich Partners Inc. survey in October which found that 52 percent of respondents without Internet access would prefer to use their TV to access the World Wide Web.

The Yankelovich survey was sponsored by WebTV Networks and WebTV Vice President of Marketing Chip Herman said he found the Dataquest data to be "quite surprising" compared with the earlier survey's findings of a preference for television access.
Lower costs, ease of use and freedom from hassles with software were examples of why Herman said a majority of consumers would prefer to use televisions, with 31 percent prefering to use PCs.

Roughly one-third of U.S. households have personal computers, although only around 10 percent of all households use online or Internet services, according to surveys. However, Baker noted the Dataquest data appearred to conflict with anecdotal feedback from some retailers that it was hard to keep sufficient stocks of the WebTV devices, marketed by Sony Corp. and Philips Electronics NV. .

WebTV devices are priced around $330 and can be hooked up to a television and a phone line to provide unlimited access to the WebTV Network access service for a $19.95 monthly fee. It is as easy to install as a video casette recorder (VCR).

WebTV provides a simplified method of surfing the Web, using a remote control device or an optional keyboard, and a recent software upgrade made it possible to listen to music and radio programming over the Internet.
